excerpt: Tycoon gives one person an AI manager plus coding, content, research and SEO agents. Free to start, then a $50/month usage wallet.
content:
Tycoon is a workspace where an AI manager runs a team of AI agents for you. You give it a goal or a project, such as growing sign-ups or launching an onboarding flow, and it writes a plan, turns it into task cards, assigns them to agents, tracks progress and asks you before anything risky. At launch the manager was called Astra, the "AI CEO"; the site now calls it Tycoon Agent. You can message it in Tycoon, iMessage, Slack or Discord.

The ready-made agents cover coding (Claude Code, a software delivery agent), content, ad and email campaigns, research, metrics, contract review and SEO, and you can build a custom agent or import a Claude Code or Codex setup. The FAQ says strategy, public publishing, customer messages, spending, production changes and legal risks go to you for approval. Pricing is usage-based: free to start with a $5 welcome credit and no card, then a $50 monthly wallet that pays for AI tokens and machine time, with no per-seat charge.

Tycoon is operated by HeyMall, Inc., a Delaware corporation, and was founded by Xiaoyin Qu, who says an earlier company, HeyBoss, was handed to an AI CEO in 2025. It launched on Product Hunt on 21 May 2026 and finished #1 for the day with 538 upvotes and 111 comments.

We have not tested Tycoon ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing, about page and terms, its Product Hunt launch page and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

team.name: Richie Cheng

use_cases: Turning a goal like "grow sign-ups this month" into a plan and tasks
Running coding work through Claude Code under one manager
Drafting SEO posts, landing pages and social posts
Market sizing, competitor research and KPI reports
Reviewing contracts and NDAs before you sign

paragraphs: Xiaoyin Qu says that a year before launch, Qu became the first human CEO to be replaced by an AI CEO, named Astra. What sounded like a stunt, Qu says, went on to help run real companies, and Tycoon is that experiment turned into a product.

Tycoon gives one person an AI CEO and a full team of AI agents: you text Astra your goals or tasks, and she turns them into structured work, assigns agents, reviews progress and asks for approval when it matters. Qu said it is built for solo founders, indie hackers and builders who want a company's output without hiring managers or coordinating everything by hand.
launch_story.attribution: Xiaoyin Qu, maker, on Product Hunt

fit: run a small software or online business alone and want agents to take on marketing, research and coding
already use Claude Code or Codex and want a manager layer above it
prefer paying for usage over per-seat subscriptions
not_fit: want a free, self-hosted tool: Tycoon is hosted and paid by usage
need refunds on unused credit: the terms say fees and token balances are not refundable
rely on CRM or project tools beyond Slack, GitHub, Stripe, GA4 and PostHog: the team said wider coverage was still coming

pricing.intro: Tycoon charges for usage rather than seats. It is free to start with a $5 welcome credit and no credit card; after that you fund a wallet. Prices are in US dollars.

plans.name: Free start
plans.detail: $5 welcome credit, no credit card required

plans.name: Wallet
plans.detail: $50 of credit a month for AI tokens (at OpenRouter rates) and machine-hours, with auto top-up; unused credit rolls over; $0 per seat

notes: Machine time is billed per second while agents run: $0.032/hr (1 GB), $0.057/hr (2 GB) or $0.106/hr (4 GB). Idle costs nothing.
You can top up as you go instead of a monthly budget.
The terms say fees are not refundable, including unused token balances and partial billing periods.

alternatives.intro: A commenter on Product Hunt compared Tycoon with the open-source Paperclip; Lindy and Relevance AI are other well-known agent platforms. Prices come from each product's own pages, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Paperclip
items.what: Open-source app that runs teams of AI agents as a company, with org charts, budgets and approvals
items.starts_at: Free, MIT-licensed and self-hosted; you pay your AI providers
items.difference: You host it and bring your own agents; Tycoon is hosted, ready-made and favours a flat team under one manager.

items.name: Lindy
items.what: AI assistant and agent builder for work tasks
items.starts_at: Free with $50 of credits for 7 days; Team from $29.99/month
items.difference: Built around automating everyday business workflows rather than a manager that runs a whole company.

items.name: Relevance AI
items.what: Platform for building teams of AI agents for companies
items.starts_at: Enterprise, talk to sales (no prices on its pricing page)
items.difference: Aimed at larger companies; Tycoon targets solo founders and small teams.

liked: One AI manager directing specialist agents, rather than one agent with a big title
asked: What the manager's review of agent work is grounded in: another AI pass, or tests and real metrics
How it differs from the open-source Paperclip

faq.a: A hosted workspace where an AI manager (Astra at launch, now called Tycoon Agent) takes your goals, plans the work and assigns it to AI agents for coding, content, campaigns, research, metrics, contracts and SEO.
It is free to start with a $5 welcome credit and no card. After that a $50 monthly wallet pays for AI tokens and machine time, with no per-seat fee. You can also top up as you go.

faq.q: Does it act without asking me?
faq.a: Only on low-risk, reversible, well-scoped work, according to its FAQ. Strategy, public publishing, customer messages, spending, production changes, legal risk and irreversible actions are sent to you for approval.

faq.q: How is it different from Paperclip?
faq.a: Paperclip is free, open source and self-hosted with your own agents. The founder said on Product Hunt that Tycoon is purpose-built for tech companies and uses a flat team under one manager rather than a deep hierarchy.

faq.q: Which tools does it connect to?
faq.a: At launch the team listed Slack, GitHub, Stripe, GA4 and PostHog. You can message the manager in iMessage, Slack or Discord and import Claude Code or Codex files.

faq.q: Can I get a refund on unused credit?
faq.a: No. Tycoon's terms say fees are not refundable, including unused token balances and partial billing periods. Cancelling takes effect at the end of the billing period.
HeyMall, Inc., a Delaware corporation, operates Tycoon. Its founder is Xiaoyin Qu.
